title: Transport of an orientation square through finite scalars and sheaf towers
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$ and a prime $\ell\ne p$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. All schemes in this statement are separated and of finite type over $k$, and all morphisms are $k$-morphisms [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use the ordinary uncompleted constant-coefficient pro-etale module derived categories and their bounded constructible finite-Tor subcategories [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules, def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf, def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. Pullbacks and tensor products are the ordinary derived operations [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-weil-derived-tensor].

Let $f:X\to Y$ be smooth separated of pure relative dimension $d\ge0$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], let $v:Y'\to Y$ be arbitrary, and put $X'=X\times_Y Y'$ with projections $u:X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to Y'$ [def-pc-base-change].
For a coefficient ring $D$ put $L_{f,D}=D_X(d)[2d]$ [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] and $\omega_{f,D}=f_D^!D_Y$, and let $e_D:u_D^*\omega_{f,D}\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{f',D}$ be the transpose of inverse compact-support exchange followed by the pulled-back counit [def-pur-co-smoothness, def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate].

(1) Let $R=\mathbf Z/\ell^r$, $r\ge1$, and let $A$ be any finite commutative ring with $\ell^rA=0$. Write $(-)_A=-\otimes_R^LA$. Use the scalar comparisons $c_f:(\omega_{f,R})_A\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{f,A}$ and $c_{f'}$, and orientations $\Pi_{f,D}:\omega_{f,D}\xrightarrow{\sim}L_{f,D}$, whose normalization is
$$\Pi_{f,A}c_f=(\Pi_{f,R})_A,\qquad\Pi_{f',A}c_{f'}=(\Pi_{f',R})_A$$
[det-sp-finite-general-ring]. Assume the mixed comparison square
$$e_Au_A^*c_f=c_{f'}(e_R)_A$$
and the orientation equation $\Pi_{f',R}e_R=u_R^*\Pi_{f,R}$. Then
$$\Pi_{f',A}e_A=u_A^*\Pi_{f,A},\qquad e_Au_A^*(\Pi_{f,A}^{-1})=\Pi_{f',A}^{-1}.$$
All identifications are the canonical derived scalar/pullback and exponent-independent Tate comparisons; no flatness of $R\to A$ is assumed.

(2) Fix a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and put $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\ell^n$. Work in the ordinary derived categories of varying-coefficient sheaf towers and their full uniformly bounded constructible finite-Tor subcategories [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers, det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian, sk-def-sp-normalized-towers]. Let $a_f:L_{f,\bullet}=A_{\bullet,X}(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{f,\bullet}$ and $a_{f'}$ be the actual tower orientations [det-sp-tower-gamma], and let $e_\bullet:u_\bullet^*\omega_{f,\bullet}\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{f',\bullet}$ be the actual tower exceptional comparison [det-sp-tower-exceptional-bc]. Suppose their exact evaluations at every $n$ satisfy $(e_\bullet)_n u_n^*(a_f)_n=(a_{f'})_n$. Then
$$e_\bullet u_\bullet^*a_f=a_{f'}$$
as morphisms in the ordinary tower derived category. More generally, exact level evaluations are jointly injective on morphisms between two sheaf towers placed in the same single degree. In particular $h=a_{f'}^{-1}e_\bullet u_\bullet^*a_f$ is determined by its evaluated identities on $A_{\bullet,X'}(d)[2d]$. This is an assertion about equally shifted sheaf towers; it does not assert faithfulness of evaluation on arbitrary derived morphisms. If $\ell$ has ramification index $e$ in $E$, the finite ring at level $n$ is $A_{E,en}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^{en}$, so the assertion includes ramified $E$ and towers without normalization.

proof.text: Precompose the finite orientation equation by pullback of scalarComparison. Rewrite with the supplied mixed square and the primed normalization. Combine the scalar functor maps and apply the supplied R-orientation equation. Naturality of scalarPullbackProEtaleIso moves the unprimed orientation to the left. The ordered Tate scalar/pullback coherence identifies the remaining line square. Finally rewrite the unprimed normalization and cancel the pulled-back scalarComparison, an isomorphism.

Postcompose the proposed inverse equation with the primed orientation. Substitute the orientation equation from the preceding step. Functoriality sends piA.inv followed by piA.hom to the identity; cancel the primed orientation.

For evaluation detection set J=singleFunctor(0) followed by shift(s). Fullness expresses the two given maps as J(f),J(g). Exact evaluation has the composite natural isomorphism J followed by derived evaluation = ordinary evaluation followed by finite singleFunctor(0) followed by shift(s). Naturality and cancellation of its components turn equality of evaluated derived maps into equality of ordinary component maps, using faithfulness of finite single and shift. Extensionality of strict system morphisms and faithfulness of the specified realization equivalence give f=g, hence equality of the original maps. The two universes t and v remain independent.

Form h=U(a.hom) followed by the actual mate and a_prime.inv. The pulled ordered-line presentation gives an isomorphism i from its source to F[0][2d]. Apply shifted_tower_evaluation_injective to i.inv followed by h followed by i.hom and the identity. At every level the supplied finite equation and functoriality reduce h to a_prime.hom followed by a_prime.inv, hence identity. Cancel i to obtain h=identity. Full-subcategory extensionality gives the same equation there; cancel a_prime.inv to recover the orientation equation and then its identity composite.

The recorded coefficient integers are a DVR and their chosen uniformizer pi generates its maximal ideal, hence pi is irreducible. The integer ell is nonzero, since it is nonzero in Q_ell and the field algebra map is injective. Choose e with ell associated to pi^e. Association invariance of emultiplicity and emultiplicity_pi(pi^e)=e identify e with the stated toNat. Associated elements generate the same principal ideal; taking (n+1)-st powers, span_singleton_pow and pow_mul give the required equality, including every ramification index.

Live still has the item unsplit. A parallel delivery of this item by Q101 (54b587ee) exists; whichever lands second is superseded at merge.

Step 1: I checked the types. Mixed square, f' normalization, functoriality of (-)_A, R-equation, naturality of lambda_u (def-sp-constant-scalar-pullback-comparison, no flatness) and f normalization give the equation. Elementary and correct.
Step 2: cancellation by an invertible map. Correct.
Step 4: joint injectivity via componentwise tower morphisms (sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers). Correct.
Step 5: h_n=1 from the hypothesis, tower pullback is levelwise exact (det-sp-tower-exceptional-bc, prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact), then step 4 with s=2d. Correct.
Step 6: (l^n)=(varpi^{en}). Correct.
Edge cases: d=0, s of either sign, A=R, A=0, non-flat Z/l^2->F_l, ramified e=2, non-normalized towers. All fine.

Fault C1/C4 in step 3: it re-derived without a citation that the derived functor of an exact functor is termwise, sends A[s] to F(A)[s] and commutes with shifts. That is the Mathlib leaf lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated. Steps 4 and 5 also used finite-level single faithfulness and derived-pullback single preservation without citing a node.
